name: Mbwela
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Angolan Mbwela essentially undescribed; only Fleisch 2009 subclassification comment surfaced, no stress statement reachable

tone_statements.citation: Silva, Janine Félix da; Rosa Maria de Lima Ribeiro & Ndonga Mfuwa. 2011. A língua bantu angolana mbwela (K17) e a busca etimológica dos bantuísmos brasileiros. PAPIA: Revista Brasileira de Estudos do Contato Linguístico 21(2): 291-302. São Paulo: USP. ISSN 0103-9415. (open copy: Zenodo, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20405833, CC-BY 4.0)
tone_statements.quote: Vale salientar que as línguas bantu são por excelência línguas tonais por isso os tons são parte primordial da língua. Porém, os tons dos exemplos demonstrados no corpo do trabalho foram postergados por ainda estarem sendo analisados de maneira profunda com a ajuda do PRAAT. [...] (p. 295:) É interessante perceber que existem algumas diferenças significativas entre o ngangela (K12b) e o mbwela (K17) que vão desde léxicos, passando pela diferença no sistema tonal, até o emparelhamento singular/ plural dos prefixos nominais (PN) de classes 9/ 10.
tone_statements.translation: It should be stressed that Bantu languages are tone languages par excellence, so the tones are a primordial part of the language. However, the tones of the examples shown in the body of this work have been deferred because they are still being analysed in depth with the help of PRAAT. [...] It is interesting to note that there are some significant differences between Ngangela (K12b) and Mbwela (K17), ranging from lexicon, through the difference in the tonal system, to the singular/plural pairing of the class 9/10 noun prefixes.
tone_statements.locator: p. 293 (end of sec. 1.1) and p. 295 (sec. 1.2 c, after the noun-class table)
tone_statements.summary: Asserts that Mbwela is tonal and that its tonal system differs from that of Ngangela K12b; tones left unmarked pending instrumental analysis, so no inventory, TBU or rules are stated.

sources.citation: Pearson, Emil. n.d. Luchazi Grammar (repr. Kalenga Chihinga 2018, luchazilanguage.blogspot.com), section 'Accent'.
sources.note: Sister language Luchazi K.13 (same Ngangela cluster): 'The stress regularly falls upon the penultimate (next to the last) syllable, except in some foreign words.' Not Mbwela.

sources.citation: Zavoni, Ntondo. 2003. Elements de description du ngangela. These de doctorat, Universite Lumiere Lyon 2 (dir. Denis Creissels). Introduction + ch. 1 Phonologie (printed pp. 12-106).
sources.note: Describes Kuvangu Ngangela (K.12b, glottocode nyem1238), listing 'mbwela' only as one of 16 Ngangela 'variantes' (intro p. 8, after Redinha). Sec. F.2 'Statut du systeme prosodique' pp. 82-85: Ngangela is 'une langue a systeme tonal restreint' where H is the only pertinent prosodic unit with behaviour 'assez proche de celui d'un pur accent'; disyllabic-stem nominals and non-finite verbs have exactly one H syllable; pausal H surfaces on the penultimate. Cluster-level; not a statement about Mbwela.

sources.citation: Kashoki, Mubanga E. & Michael Mann. 1978. A general sketch of the Bantu languages of Zambia. In Ohannessian & Kashoki (eds.), Language in Zambia. London: IAI. (UNZA DSpace text)
sources.note: Mentions only the ZAMBIAN Mbwela ('Mbwela see Lukolwe', Nkoya group) - a different language from mbwe1238; areal remark that Zambian languages have even stress with slight penultimate prominence. Not applicable.

sources.citation: Magalhaes, Antonio Miranda. 1922. Manual de linguas indigenas de Angola. Loanda: Imprensa Nacional de Angola. (Rosetta Project excerpts on archive.org: Indice + Parte I 'Fonetica'; Glottolog 99449 language code includes 'Ganguela (Ganguela/Ambuela/..)')
sources.note: General orthographic convention for Kimbundu/Umbundu only: acute accent used 'para indicar a silaba predominante das palavras esdruxulas' (i.e. accent written only on proparoxytones). Ganguela/Ambuela treated only in Part V (not in the excerpt); nothing Mbwela-specific.

sources.citation: Johnston, Harry H. 1919-1922. A Comparative Study of the Bantu and Semi-Bantu Languages, vols. 1-2. Oxford: Clarendon. (no. 86b 'Western Mbwela (Ambwela)'; no. 87a 'Mbwela' = Zambian Nkoya-Mbwela)
sources.note: Nothing specific to 86b; only the work-wide transcription convention (vol. 1 front matter, the scanned text): accent 'is so normally and frequently on the penultimate syllable that the accent is only employed when an exception to the prevailing rule in Bantu transfers the voice-pitch to the first, last, or other syllable'. 86b data are second-hand from Serpa Pinto/Capello & Ivens.

sources.citation: Baum, Hermann (red. Otto Warburg). 1903. Kunene-Sambesi-Expedition. Berlin: Kolonial-Wirtschaftliches Komitee. (archive.org kunenesambesiexp00baum; Glottolog 61733 tags it Mbwela [mfu])
sources.note: Nothing; travel/botanical/zoological report, no vocabulary or language section found by a full-text search for stress/accent (Sprachprobe/Woerter/Betonung/Akzent/Mbuela/Ambuella all absent).

sources.citation: Lecomte, Ernesto. 1897. Plan'alto do sul de Angola: missoes portuguezas Caconda, Catoco, Bihe e Bailundo. Lisboa: Sociedade de Geographia. (archive.org planaltodosulde00lecogoog)
sources.note: Nothing; mission report, mentions his forthcoming work on the language of the 'Vimbundu e Vanganguella' (p. 24) only.

sources.citation: Serpa Pinto, Alexandre de. 1881. How I Crossed Africa, from the Atlantic to the Indian Ocean, through unknown countries. 2 vols. London: Sampson Low, Marston, Searle & Rivington. (archive.org scanned howicrossedafric01serp / 02serp)
sources.note: Nothing. Only language remark (vol. 2 Supplementary chapter pp. 108-109): 'Three of the above races, namely, the Quimbandes, Luchazes, and Ambuellas, speak the same language, the Ganguella, with trifling modifications.' Johnston 1919's column 86b 'Western Mbwela (Ambwela)' derives from this and Capello & Ivens.

sources.citation: Silva, Janine Félix da; Rosa Maria de Lima Ribeiro & Ndonga Mfuwa. 2011. A língua bantu angolana mbwela (K17) e a busca etimológica dos bantuísmos brasileiros. PAPIA: Revista Brasileira de Estudos do Contato Linguístico 21(2): 291-302. São Paulo: USP. ISSN 0103-9415. (open copy: Zenodo, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20405833, CC-BY 4.0)
sources.quote: Vale salientar que as línguas bantu são por excelência línguas tonais por isso os tons são parte primordial da língua. Porém, os tons dos exemplos demonstrados no corpo do trabalho foram postergados por ainda estarem sendo analisados de maneira profunda com a ajuda do PRAAT. [...] (p. 295:) É interessante perceber que existem algumas diferenças significativas entre o ngangela (K12b) e o mbwela (K17) que vão desde léxicos, passando pela diferença no sistema tonal, até o emparelhamento singular/ plural dos prefixos nominais (PN) de classes 9/ 10.
sources.locator: p. 293 (end of sec. 1.1) and p. 295 (sec. 1.2 c, after the noun-class table)
sources.note: First-hand sketch (vowels, consonant inventory, 18 noun-class prefixes) from elicitation with a native speaker. On tone it states only that Mbwela is a tone language whose tones are 'parte primordial da língua', that tone marking of the examples was deliberately withheld pending Praat analysis (p. 293), and that Mbwela differs from Ngangela (K12b) inter alia 'pela diferença no sistema tonal' (p. 295). No tone inventory, tone-bearing unit or tone rules are given; nothing on stress/accent.
sources.venue: PAPIA: Revista Brasileira de Estudos do Contato Linguístico
